title: ephemeral-oncall-momentum-and-pager-decay-suggester
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds ephemeral on-call momentum metric and a probabilistic pager-decay scheduler; introduces a suggestion endpoint and CLI helper to propose quiet windows during high-noise periods.
description:
Summary: Introduces an "oncall_momentum" metric that quantifies recent alert activity velocity and a probabilistic 'pager decay' scheduler that recommends temporary, short-duration quiet windows when on-call momentum indicates alert noise rather than actionable incidents. Motivation: recurring noisy alerts during low-impact degradations disrupt responders and increase toil; we need a conservative, observable mechanism to reduce unnecessary wake-ups while preserving SLO-driven escalation for real incidents.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a lightweight streaming metric (oncall_momentum) computed from alert ingestion rates, signal half-life, and responder acknowledgements; implements a pager-decay policy that produces probabilistic suppressions (throttle decisions) with auditability; exposes an HTTP suggestion endpoint (/v1/oncall/suggestions) and a CLI command (sloctl suggest-quiet) for engineers to preview recommended quiet windows; wires metric and decision traces into the existing tracing and audit logs.

Checklist: - [x] Metric computation implementation and tests - [x] Pager-decay decision engine and deterministic mode for tests - [x] API surface and auth (token-scoped) - [x] CLI help and basic e2e smoke test - [x] Docs: behavior, tuning guide, and safe-fallbacks - [x] Safety gates: auto-disable when critical alert patterns detected - [x] Telemetry: expose histograms and sampled decision logs

Commits (high level): * feat(metrics): oncall_momentum stream with exponential decay window * feat(scheduler): probabilistic pager_decay engine and deterministic mode * api: suggestion endpoint + OpenAPI docs + auth scope checks * cli: sloctl suggest-quiet implementation and output formatting * docs: quiet-windows.md with tuning examples * tests: unit + integration fixtures for simulated alert bursts * ci: add new lint/test jobs to matrix

Files changed (high level): src/metrics/momentum.py - core metric logic and streaming window helpers src/scheduler/pager_decay.py - decision engine, probabilistic sampler, and safety checks api/routes/oncall_suggestions.py - new route and request validation cli/sloctl/suggest.py - CLI shim and formatting lib/probability/utils.py - small helpers for reproducible sampling docs/quiet-windows.md - behavior, examples, and pitfalls tests/test_momentum.py tests/test_pager_decay.py tests/e2e/suggest_smoke.sh .github/workflows/ci.yaml - add matrix entry for suggestion smoke test

Design notes and safety: The scheduler operates in "observe" mode by default for the hosted service (no automatic suppression). Customers using the private installer can opt-in to execute suppressions via an operator-approved toggle. The decision logic is conservative: it requires (a) momentum above a tunable threshold, (b) absence of high-severity alerts matching incident rules, and (c) a minimum observation window of 2 minutes. Sampled decisions are logged to audit with input vectors to enable post-hoc analysis and regression tests.

Backward compatibility: API additions are additive. The suggestion endpoint requires a new OAuth scope (oncall:suggest) — calling without scope returns 403. CLI defaults favor dry-run output.

Review conversation (compact transcript): Lena Ortiz (reviewer, 2026-02-16): "Nice direction. Two asks: (1) make the half-life configurable via runtime config (not compile-time), and (2) add an explicit opt-out for customers that rely on exact PagerDuty semantics." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-16): "Agree on both; added runtime config and opted to make the opt-out flag sticky in customer prefs. See momentum.py lines 42-68 and api route for pref check." Samir Gupta (reviewer, 2026-02-17): "Can we avoid non-determinism in tests? The probabilistic sampler should be seedable." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-17): "Added deterministic mode and injected RNG seed in tests; included test harness in test_pager_decay.py." Priya Nambiar (reviewer, 2026-02-18): "Docs are great. One small UX nit: CLI output should show rationale for suggestion (dominant signal)." Maya Chen (author reply, 2026-02-18): "Added explanation block to CLI output that lists top-2 contributing signals and their weights."

CI and iteration: Initial CI run showed a flaky e2e that relied on wall-clock timing (2026-02-17); fixed by switching to simulated clock in e2e harness and re-ran CI. Final CI status: pass on all checks (unit, lint, integration, e2e smoke).

Testing and observability: Unit tests cover core math (edge cases for zero alerts), integration tests run simulated alert streams against local scheduler, and e2e smoke runs the suggestion endpoint and verifies JSON schema. Added tracing spans for metric ingestion and decision evaluation and a sampling hook to write sampled decisions to the audit log for 0.1% of decisions by default.

Operational runbook excerpt (included in docs): If customers observe more missed critical alerts after enabling suppressions, toggle the feature off and collect sampled decision logs (sloctl collect-samples) and open a support ticket with SUP-9876.

Related: ENG-4821 implements long-term oncall analytics; PM-119 tracks the user research on on-call noise thresholds.

Merge notes: Squash and merge after approvals; forward-port note for release branch v1.28.1.
merge_commit_message: Introduce oncall_momentum metric and pager-decay suggester; add API and CLI; docs and tests. Closes ENG-4821.
post_merge_actions: backport to release/v1.28.x, notify ops slack #oncall-tooling, and schedule a short post-deploy bake on staging with simulated bursts
notes_for_release_notes: Added a conservative suggestion system to recommend temporary quiet windows during noisy alert periods; no automatic suppression enabled by default for hosted customers.
motivation: Reduce on-call fatigue from noisy alerts while preserving incident detection guarantees and providing clear audit trails for any suppression decisions.
